summary:
Followed the open lead with a real producer path instead of more reading, and requested the fixed execution that answers the registered gap (gap-2, shouldSnapshot's unsigned delta).

Harness (draft/assurance_snapshot_underflow.go, mapped to the package test file by the controller): MakeCluster(3) with SnapshotInterval=40ms, SnapshotThreshold=20, TrailingLogs=5; 60 warm commands so every node snapshots and compacts; c.Disconnect on one follower plus 140 further commands so the leader's log compacts past that follower's next index; c.FullyConnect so the follower recovers through the real InstallSnapshot handler; then the recovered node is isolated again so any later snapshot must come from its own snapshot goroutine. window_start/window_end emit raw operands (snapshot index, newest snapshot ID, log store last index, last snapshot index, should_snapshot(), applied index, distinct snapshot IDs, applied delta, tick count) for the recovered node and for the leader over the same 900ms window, with the derived boolean snapshot_created_without_new_entries.

Comparisons requested: recovered node's window_end shows snapshot_created_without_new_entries true (applicability: applied_delta 0 and should_snapshot true), and the leader control in the same window shows false. Requirement and responsibility are anchored at shouldSnapshot (snapshot.go:106-120), runSnapshots (snapshot.go:72-102), installSnapshot (raft.go:1814-1950) and compactLogsWithTrailing (snapshot.go:216-240).

Native local feedback (explicitly not retained evidence, and flagged as such in the investigation's limitations): the run reached the state of interest — snapshot index 202 above log store last index 62 after reconnect — and over the 900ms window the recovered node produced 16 distinct snapshot IDs at the same index 202 with applied_delta 0 while should_snapshot stayed true, against 1 distinct ID, should_snapshot false for the leader. The question stays paused with resume conditions so the conclusion can be written from the controller's own receipt rather than from my local run; validation of these bytes returns valid:true.
